# `terraform stacks configuration show` reference

Use the `terraform stacks configuration show` command to show details of a configuration.

## Usage

```shell-session
$ terraform stacks <global-stacks-flags> configuration show <options>
```

## Description

The `terraform stacks configuration show` command retrieves relevant information for a given configuration, including its deployment groups, ingress attributes, and diagnostic help . 

You can identify the target configuration either by providing a configuration ID directly, or by specifying the organization name, project name, and Stack name combination. When name-based targeting is used, the latest configuration for that stack is shown.
## Options

- `-organization-name`: The name of the organization to target.
    - Optional when using `-stack-id`, required when using name-based targeting.
    - String data type.
    - Overrides the ENV VAR `TF_STACKS_ORGANIZATION_NAME` if provided.
- `-project-name`: The name of the project to target.
    - Optional when using `-stack-id`, required when using name-based targeting.
    - String data type.
    - Overrides the ENV VAR `TF_STACKS_PROJECT_NAME` if provided.
- `-stack-name`: The name of the stack to target.
    - Optional when using `-stack-id`, required when using name-based targeting.
    - String data type.
    - Overrides the ENV VAR `TF_STACKS_STACK_NAME` if provided.
- `-configuration-id`: The ID of the configuration to show.
    - Optional (but required when not using name-based targeting).
    - String data type.
    - Has precedence over the latest configuration of the stack provided in named args.
- `-json`: Output results in JSON format.
    - Optional.
    - Boolean flag.
    - Default is false (human-readable output).

## Examples

The following command shows details of a configuration for a Stack using organization, project, and Stack names:

```shell-session
$ terraform stacks configuration show -organization-name my-org -project-name my-project -stack-name my-stack
```

The following command shows the details of a configuration using the configuration ID:

```shell-session
$ terraform stacks configuration show -configuration-id stack-abc123def456
```

The following command shows the details of a configuration and outputs the result in JSON format:

```shell-session
$ terraform stacks configuration show -configuration-id stack-abc123def456 -json
```
